source.title: Inheritance of Refusals from Abliterated Models

page_placements.theme: Refusal changes pass to students through distillation

record.file_problem: none; the full post text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It compares refusal rates for an original teacher and a released abliterated checkpoint, and measures refusal behavior after students are trained on the edited model’s rollouts. It does not reproduce the original activation-direction measurement or intervention.
record.gate_note: The post reports refusal outcomes for original and abliterated models and for students trained on their rollouts. It does not identify, measure, add, or project out a difference-in-means direction. Fact-level lie and coherence results are not rows because they do not measure a claim-version outcome. Results cited from Conmy are not included.
record.test_reason: The post compares refusal rates of a released abliterated checkpoint (Huihui-Qwen3.5-9B-abliterated) with the original Qwen 3.5 9B. It uses a new setting: China-sensitive censorship questions plus 1,000 unrelated OLMo prompts. That bears on V2, practical removal in released models. It does not identify, ablate or add a difference-in-means direction. The distillation experiments measure refusal behaviour inherited through rollouts, not transfer of a direction, so they fit no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The author concludes that the abliterated teacher's reduced refusal transfers cleanly to a first-generation student, cross-family and same-family, and persists weakly into a second generation. The author cautions that low student coherence makes judged refusals and lies unreliable, and is not confident the results hold at scale.
record.recipe_differences: The author used an existing released abliterated checkpoint rather than performing the original activation-direction intervention, then studied rollout distillation and refusal rates. Local training and serving differed somewhat from the released Llama recipe; no original Qwen control lineage was rerun.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differed by prompt set and transfer generation: refusal rates were reported separately for China-sensitive questions and unrelated OLMo prompts, and refusals returned in the second-generation student. Student coherence was also a stated interpretive concern.

fits_no_version.finding: Students fine-tuned on unrelated rollouts from the abliterated teacher refuse less on China-sensitive questions. Cross-family Llama went from 7.11% (original-teacher control) to 0.00%; same-family Qwen 4B went from 3.78% to 0.44%. A second-generation Llama student rose to 4.89%. Student coherence is low throughout.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reduced refusal from an abliteration edit is inherited behaviourally by students distilled on the edited model's unrelated rollouts, weakening over generations.

record.problems: The author did not perform the abliteration edit, did not rerun the original Qwen control lineage, and reports no uncertainty estimates. The Llama students had low coherence, which the author says may cause refusal judgments to be misleading. No downstream intelligence or general capability benchmarks were run, and the author says the experiment was not tested at scale.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant refusal rows left out. Fact-level lies, reference-fact mentions, and coherence scores were not included because they do not measure the refusal outcomes named by the tested versions.

untested.parts: Refusal of harmful requests, as opposed to China-sensitive censorship and benign prompts. Not tested: how the edit was made, other released models, and general capability benchmarks.
Entirely untested: no direction is computed, ablated or added.
Untested: direction transfer across languages, variants or base-to-instruct is not measured. Distillation results are behavioural only.
Entirely untested: thinking was disabled, and reasoning-model experiments were explicitly not run.

missing.what: Teacher coherence: original 98.49 vs abliterated 94.30 (Gemini judge, 0–100). This bears on whether other abilities are kept after the released edit.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: the study is a new-setting behavioural check of a released abliterated checkpoint, not a different method on the direction itself. V6 labels were removed because the distillation measures behavioural inheritance, not the direction carrying across models. The post does not describe how the Huihui checkpoint was edited, so its link to the difference-in-means ablation rests on the 'abliterated' label. Refusals here are mostly censorship and benign-prompt refusals, not harmful-request refusals. There is a single judge (Gemini 3 Flash) and no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is identified or ablated or added; effects on other abilities are not tested.
The author did not perform the weight edit. The post evaluates a released abliterated checkpoint against an original teacher; it does not test other released models or general capability.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation is tested.
No affine, cone, or multiple-direction account is tested.
No separate measure of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.

The post tests transfer of refusal behavior associated with an abliterated checkpoint through distillation, not whether the same direction itself transfers. It does not test cross-language transfer or transfer from a base model to an instruct model.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages for whether a removable direction exists.
No reasoning-model test; the author says reasoning-model experiments were not performed.

relation.reason: The study reports its own refusal rates for the abliterated checkpoint against the original, and these bear on whether V2 holds. It does not only use the model as a tool.

tranche.reason: The teacher comparison (released abliterated vs original Qwen 3.5 9B) is a refusal-rate result on V2 in a new setting: censorship questions, a third-party checkpoint, and no edit by the author. It is a side check in a distillation study, not a method aimed at the abliteration question, so T3 fits better than the reader's T2.

source_check.notes: The pack lists verdicts without [lN] ids, so no_id_1 and no_id_2 are placeholders by position (supports, then limits_scope). The text calls the 4B student 'Qwen 3.5 4B Base' but links Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Base. The study uses a single judge (Gemini 3 Flash Preview), gives no uncertainty, and never says how the Huihui checkpoint was edited.

statements.correction: lw:E7Q: Huihui-Qwen3.5-9B-abliterated vs original Qwen 3.5 9B, 90 China-sensitive questions x5, refusals 66/450 (14.67%) -> 1/450 (0.22%). Judge: Gemini 3 Flash Preview. Counts only, no statistical test or uncertainty. Teacher rollouts at temperature 1; fine-tuning seed 42; evaluation temperature not stated.
statements.problem: The lw:E7Q numbers are right. But the item calls its studies paired evaluations 'with statistical tests', and lw:E7Q has none: it gives raw counts only, and the 'why' leaves out that its uncertainty is n. 'One temperature and one seed' is not stated for lw:E7Q's evaluation sampling.

statements.correction: Llama 3.2 3B: Conmy's released control (trained on original-Qwen rollouts) 32/450 (7.11%) vs local student trained on abliterated-Qwen rollouts 0/450 (0.00%); coherence 40.81 vs 38.98. Qwen 4B base: untrained 17/450 (3.78%) vs trained on abliterated rollouts 2/450 (0.44%); coherence 95.39 -> 82.59; there is no original-Qwen-trained Qwen 4B control. The author warns that low coherence makes judged refusals unreliable.
statements.problem: All numbers are in the text, but the two comparisons are not alike. For Qwen 4B, 3.78% is the untrained bare base model, not a student trained on original-Qwen rollouts, so that drop doesn't isolate abliteration. Cited row r5 (bare Llama, 76.22%) holds none of the statement's numbers, and the rows behind 0.00%, 3.78% and 0.44% are not cited.
